title: Variables and types
content: Variables bind names to values. Types describe value categories and influence operations: integers, floating-point numbers, strings, booleans, collections, and objects. Type errors often occur when incompatible operations are attempted.
example: age = 16 stores an integer; name = 'Caio' stores text.

title: Control flow
content: Control flow selects or repeats execution. Conditionals choose a branch based on a boolean expression; loops repeat while iterating over items or while a condition holds. Ensure loops have a clear termination condition.
cautions: Infinite loops can freeze a program; test boundary conditions.

title: Functions
content: A function is a reusable unit that may accept parameters and return a value. Separate input, computation, and side effects where practical. Give functions one clear responsibility and document expectations.
example: def add(a, b): return a + b

title: Data structures
content: Choose data structures based on operations: lists/arrays preserve order and support indexed access; dictionaries/maps associate keys with values; sets store unique members; tuples often represent fixed groupings. Consider complexity and mutation behavior.

title: Algorithmic complexity
content: Big-O describes how resource use grows with input size, ignoring constants and lower-order terms. O(1) constant, O(log n) logarithmic, O(n) linear, O(n log n) commonly efficient sorting, O(n²) quadratic. Big-O is a growth model, not a precise runtime prediction.

title: Debugging workflow
content: A disciplined debugging cycle: reproduce the failure; read the full error and stack trace; isolate a minimal case; inspect assumptions and state; make one targeted change; rerun the failing case and relevant regression tests; record the root cause.
cautions: Do not blindly change multiple things at once or hide exceptions before understanding them.

title: Testing
content: Tests compare observed behavior with expected behavior. Unit tests isolate small functions; integration tests verify components working together; regression tests prevent previously fixed bugs returning. Include typical, boundary, invalid, and failure cases.

title: APIs and HTTP
content: An API defines a contract for software interaction. HTTP requests have methods, headers, and optional bodies; responses have status, headers, and content. JSON is a common data format. Validate input and handle status codes and timeouts.
cautions: Do not assume a successful network response or trust unvalidated remote input.

title: Git basics
content: Version control records project history. A commit is a snapshot; branches allow parallel changes; merging integrates histories. Inspect status and diffs before committing, and use meaningful commit messages.
cautions: A commit is not a backup by itself; push to a separate remote and keep backups when needed.

title: Code readability and modularity
content: Readable code uses clear names, small cohesive modules, consistent style, explicit interfaces, and limited hidden side effects. Refactor behavior-preservingly: add tests, make a small change, then verify.
cautions: Avoid duplicating logic and avoid overengineering abstractions before they are useful.
